title.rendered: Blessed Are the Meek: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.” A morning devotional on the quiet strength Jesus called blessed.

content.rendered:
The Old Testament calls one man “very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.” That man was Moses. Meekness is not weakness. Just ask the man who stood before Pharaoh, parted the Red Sea, and led two million people out of slavery.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, August 30, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Blessed are the meek, For they shall inherit the earth.”
Matthew 5:5 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Numbers 12:3 makes a startling claim about Moses. The verse reads, in the King James rendering that has echoed through centuries of English preaching, that Moses was “very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.” Not the strongest. Not the boldest. The meekest. And yet this is the same Moses who stood before Pharaoh, called down the plagues, parted the Red Sea, led two million former slaves through the wilderness for forty years, and shaped the entire nation of Israel by the direct word of God. Meekness, in the biblical sense, has almost nothing to do with what the modern world assumes the word means. Meekness is not weakness. Meekness is what strength looks like when it has fully submitted to God.

Jesus takes that ancient understanding and places it at the centre of the third beatitude. “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.” He is continuing the Sermon on the Mount, unveiling the character of the Kingdom people. First, the poor in spirit. Then, those who mourn. Now, the meek. And attached to the meek is one of the most extraordinary promises in the entire Bible. Not a small reward. Not a spiritual reward. The earth itself. The whole planet. The meek inherit what the ambitious spend their lives trying to seize.

The Greek word Jesus uses for “meek” is praus. In classical Greek, it was used to describe a wild horse that had been broken to the saddle. The horse still had all its power. Its muscles were unchanged. Its speed was undiminished. But the strength was now under the control of the rider. That is meekness. Not a horse with no power. A horse whose power has been submitted. The believer who is meek is not a believer with nothing to offer. It is a believer whose whole strength, whole intelligence, whole personality has been placed under the hand of the Master.

The Passion Translation renders the beatitude with striking clarity: “What contentment floods those who yield their entire being to God! For they will inherit the earth” (Matthew 5:5 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Blessed (happy, blithesome, joyous, spiritually prosperous—with life-joy and satisfaction in God’s favor and salvation, regardless of their outward conditions) are the meek (the mild, patient, long-suffering), for they shall inherit the earth!” (Matthew 5:5 AMPC). Notice the outcome. The meek do not fight for the earth. The meek do not scheme for the earth. The meek do not have to. The earth is given to them, at the right time, by the Father who holds the whole thing in His hand.

Jesus Himself models the beatitude perfectly. He says of Himself in Matthew 11:29, “I am gentle and lowly in heart”, using the same root word praus. The same Jesus who overturned tables in the Temple, spoke truth to Herod, and refused to bow to any earthly power, described His own inner life as meek. The strength was there. It was fully surrendered to the Father. And the earth He inherits, at the end of all things, is the whole created order remade in righteousness. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, the invitation of the beatitude is to lay down the exhausting need to seize your own portion. Submit your strength to the Master. Trust the Father to give you what is yours. The meek inherit the earth.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that meekness is not weakness. It is strength submitted to Your hand. Today I bring You my strength, my intelligence, my personality, my ambition, my will. I lay it all under Your rein. I refuse to fight for my own portion today. I trust You to give me what is mine, at the right time, in the right way. The meek inherit the earth because the earth is Yours to give. I walk in that today. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am meek in Christ. My strength is submitted to the Father. I do not fight for my own portion today. The Father gives the earth to the meek, and I walk in that promise.
